what: EthicalVerdicts published by the Module 5 gate (mrs_ethical_gate) on /mrs/verdict for the same two-robot plan, with and without a person beside robot_b's waiting spot. With the person, S-2 (human crowding) rejects the plan: both robots would be within R of the person at the same time, though either robot alone would be allowed (N = 1). Without the person, the plan is approved.

how_produced.machine: M2 MacBook, macOS 26.5.2, ROS 2 Jazzy (RoboStack conda env mrs-ethics), no simulation
how_produced.plan_publisher: ros2 run mrs_common sample_plan_pub --ros-args -p sample:=valid_two_robots.json -p period:=1.0 (the first verdict of each run is kept)
how_produced.notes: R = 1.5 m and N = 1 are placeholders, neither measured nor from a standard. latency_ms is the gate's own measurement of one decide() call on this machine, for this one message.

scenario.map: src/fleet_checker/test/fixtures/samples_world.yaml (fleet_checker's test map for the Module 1 sample plans; not a mrs_sim world)

people.where: east_hall, 1.1 m from corridor_2, where robot_b waits for robot_a

tasks.justification: Go through the narrow passage first while it is free.
Wait outside the narrow passage until robot_a is through.

plan.rationale: Both robots need the narrow passage; robot_a goes first and robot_b waits outside it.

verdict.rationale: Plan rejected: robot_a and robot_b would be within 1.5 m of person_1 (nearest node corridor_2) at the same time, but at most 1 robot may be. Propose a new plan that follows the constraints.

constraints.text: robot_a and robot_b would be within 1.5 m of person_1 (nearest node corridor_2) at the same time, but at most 1 robot may be, and making robot_a wait for robot_b does not fix it: the tasks would wait for each other in a cycle. Change the plan so that robot_a keeps more than 1.5 m from person_1 while robot_b is there.

verdict.rationale: Plan approved: no rule violations found.
